passage:
On the second Sunday of the month Usha took the train from her Pune flat to her parents' house. Over lunch her aunt said, "Why live alone when there's a room here?" Usha smiled and passed the salad. "Because I like my own place. But look at our whiteboard." On it, in Usha's handwriting: Usha pays the monthly grocery order and calls on odd days. Her brother Chaitanya handles the society meetings and bank visits and calls on even days. Wednesday evenings were Usha's pottery class, and nobody phoned then unless it mattered.
"We agreed this in March," Usha said. "If it gets heavy for anyone, we change it." Her father tapped the board and nodded, as if it were a contract everyone had signed.

qa.q: What day of the month did Usha visit her parents' house?
qa.a: Usha visited on the second Sunday of the month.

qa.q: What was Usha feeling when her aunt asked why she lived alone?
qa.a: She felt calm and sure of herself, shown by her smile and her explaining plainly that she likes her own place.

qa.q: What made Usha's arrangement fair to the whole family?
qa.a: The duties were agreed openly and split between Usha and her brother Chaitanya, with free evenings kept for Usha and a promise to change the plan if it gets heavy.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya see the whiteboard plan?
qa.a: Chaitanya likely finds it fair, since his tasks are written next to Usha's and the calls alternate on odd and even days.

grounding: A young adult supports family in agreed ways while keeping her own life, with duties freely chosen and fairly shared.

passage:
"Papa, I'm not saying this because I have to," said Lavanya, setting down the tea tray.
"I don't want you to feel bound," said Santosh.
"I feel chosen, not bound. I'll come every Saturday and take Amma to her walk in the park. Thursday evenings are for my pottery class. Those stay mine."
"And if the week is heavy?"
"Then I say so, and you don't sulk." She grinned.
"I never sulk," Santosh said.
"Papa."
"Fine, a little." He laughed. "And your brother?"
"Sunday lunch at his place, and he does the bank visits. I already asked him."
Amma called from the balcony, "Write it on the calendar so we all remember."
Lavanya took the marker.

qa.q: Which day did Lavanya say she would come every week?
qa.a: Lavanya said she would come every Saturday.

qa.q: What is Lavanya feeling about the duties she takes on?
qa.a: She feels chosen and willing, not bound, and also protective of her time, as she keeps Thursday evenings for pottery.

qa.q: What made the arrangement work for both Lavanya and her family?
qa.a: They agreed the days openly, kept her Thursday evenings, shared duties with her brother and said they would speak up if the week got heavy.

qa.q: Why might Santosh say he does not want Lavanya to feel bound?
qa.a: Santosh seems to want her help to be freely given and not an obligation, which is why he asks what happens if the week is heavy.

grounding: A young adult supports family in agreed ways while keeping her own time, and duty is freely chosen and fairly shared.
